Resolves #18461
Refs #18456
Refs #18674
Refs #18680
Refs #18208

Workstation now boots through a **793-line composition entrypoint**. Resident markup, topology controls and the status readout have focused view owners; the existing Feed store owns its single producer and timer. App-specific vessel policy lives in `VesselWorkspace`, using the existing engine Group and native-window owners. Callers read feed counters from the store, and the README explains ordinary boot, optional playback and creator/borrower cleanup.

Evidence: L3 achieved and required for this consumer composition change. Final-head boot/reload, real-pointer transfer, pane/DOM identity, undo/redo and long-title checks pass at `264d742b74c6e6394399155b085518b0cec2b9c8`, rebased onto `dev@0bab574360` including the merged stand-in identity repair. Existing broader journey failures remain attributed below; this PR does not claim to repair them or approve a film.

## Deltas from ticket

The root uses an app-specific `VesselWorkspace` base, discussed with the prior composition owner at intake. It owns popup policy and native-resource teardown; presentation and data production use ordinary view/store classes. No engine contract or configuration schema is introduced.

The return/header repair in PR #18684 is separate merge-order work. Its vessel-method changes belong in `VesselWorkspace`, and its Reset change remains on `Workspace`; whichever PR lands second carries those deltas. The existing `retainTopology` override remains with #18208. The operator's toolbar reduction is parked separately in #18680. These are not silent scope additions to this refactor.

Change class: capability (`feat`) — separately operable Feed lifecycle and focused view owners. `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; commit hooks, parsing, diff checks and `check-file-sizes -- --base origin/dev` passed. The rebased head gets a fresh CI run before reviewer assignment.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #18461 body and its six ACs; the changed-file list; `dev` source of `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`; the sibling `apps/workstation/view/` and `store/` neighbours; Memory Core sweep on Workstation decomposition, which surfaced @neo-opus-grace's #18304 measurement that 34 methods left the façade and not one returned as a wrapper. The PR body was read only afterwards, as a claim to verify.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** The host becomes a thin composer and each extracted owner has one reason to change. It must not hardcode engine dock specifics into the app layer, and each new owner should carry its own test isolation. The failure mode to hunt was **relocation rather than decomposition** — a god object changing address, with a wrapper layer appearing where the methods used to be.
*   **Patch Verdict:** **Matches, and corrected my expectation on one point.** I predicted from the file list that a 1,584-line `VesselWorkspace` arriving with no dedicated spec would read as a relocated monolith. Two pieces of evidence moved me. First, its 27 methods are uniformly vessel-lifecycle concerns — `tearOutWorkspaceKey`, `initializeVesselResources`, `createVesselWorkspaceDocument`, `resolveTearOutVessel`, `retireVesselWorkspaceTarget`, `afterTearOutWindowDisconnect` — so it is a themed owner, not the generic helper AC-2 forbids. Second, and this is the part I had backwards: **AC-2's prohibition on "wrapper-per-method" is precisely what rules out composing these away.** The methods are engine template-hook overrides (`beforeRefreshDockWorkspace`, `getRefreshOptions`, `resolveLivePane`, `reparentDockPane`); composing them out requires a delegation layer, which is the wrapper-per-method the AC bans. A base class is the shape these ACs permit, and presentation and data genuinely *are* composed — `ResidentComponent` and `StatusComponent` extend `component.Base`, `TopologyToolbar` extends `toolbar.Base`, and `Feed` is an ordinary store.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The body declares the base class openly at its Deltas section rather than letting the word "compose" in the title carry an inheritance change unannounced, and it separates what it does not claim — no film approval, no repair of the broader journey failures, baseline attribution for pre-existing reds.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** The extracted owner arrives without a spec of its own, and the extraction was the moment that became visible. At the exact head, sampling eight `VesselWorkspace` methods against the owning `Workspace.spec.mjs`: `resolveTearOutVessel` 1 mention, `createVesselWorkspaceDocument` 3, `getPopupStates` 1, and **zero** for `retireVesselWorkspaceTarget`, `reparentDockPane`, `afterTearOutWindowDisconnect`, `resolveVesselConversionSourceRect` and `admitDockPopOut`.

This is **pre-existing and not introduced here** — those methods carried the same coverage while they lived on `Workspace`, and per guide §7.5 authors own existing non-CI coverage rather than being asked to reconstruct it. The vessel paths are also exercised at the e2e tier, which your receipt names. So this is not a Required Action. It is the observation that moving 806 code lines into a named owner makes "what covers this owner?" answerable for the first time, and the answer today is "its subclass's spec, partially." Worth a line on #18461's parent or a follow-up leaf rather than this PR.

**Documented search — what I looked for and cleared:**

- **A broken prototype-chain assumption.** Inserting `VesselWorkspace` deepens the chain by one, and the diff replaces `Object.getPrototypeOf(Workspace.prototype)` with an explicit `DockWorkspace.prototype`. I swept for other depth-dependent walks: at the head there are **zero** `getPrototypeOf` occurrences left in that spec, and the only other site (`WorkstationTabDragLabelOverlapNL:73`) reads `target?.prototype || Object.getPrototypeOf(target)`, which resolves a target's own prototype rather than walking up a level, so the new layer does not reach it.
- **A mishandled size baseline.** The diff *removes* a row while a large new module arrives, which looks wrong until measured. `VesselWorkspace` is **806 code lines** against the guard's 1,000 target, so it correctly needs no row, and `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` dropping from its 1,291 baseline is why that row goes. `check-size` passes at the head.
- **Rhetorical overshoot on "compose".** Verified below; the body names the base class explicitly.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):**

- [x] PR description: framing matches the diff. The title says "compose the app through focused view and data owners", and the composed half is real. The inherited half is declared in the body's own words — "The root uses an app-specific `VesselWorkspace` base, discussed with the prior composition owner at intake" — rather than hidden behind the title's verb.
- [x] Anchor & Echo summaries: `Workspace`'s class docblock states "this class owns only composition and story", which the 793-line root substantiates.
- [x] `[RETROSPECTIVE]` tag: none claimed.
- [x] Linked anchors: #18684, #18208 and #18680 are cited as separate merge-order and parked work, not as authority borrowed for this change.

**Findings:** Pass.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: An acceptance criterion that forbids wrapper-per-method is also, implicitly, a criterion that permits inheritance for template-hook overrides. Engine hooks cannot be composed out without the delegation layer the AC bans, so "compose the app" and "use an app-specific base for hook policy" are not in tension here — they partition on whether the responsibility is a *hook override* or a *presentation/data owner*. That partition is the reusable idea in this cut.
